records.title: Anti-neuroinflammatory polyprenylated acylphloroglucinols from Hypericum patulum: LC-MS/MS-guided isolation, semi-synthesis, and TLR4 inhibition
records.source_title: Anti-neuroinflammatory polyprenylated acylphloroglucinols from Hypericum patulum: LC-MS/MS-guided isolation, semi-synthesis, and TLR4 inhibition
records.abstract: Researchers isolated 45 polyprenylated acylphloroglucinol compounds, including 13 previously unreported analogs, from Hypericum patulum. Fourteen compounds reduced nitric oxide production in BV-2 cells. Further experiments implicated TLR4-associated signaling, and a compound was studied in a zebrafish model. These are preclinical findings and cannot establish human benefit.
records.relevance_reason: Primary botanical isolation and cell-signaling study with explicit preclinical relevance limits.
records.study_design: Chemical isolation, cell culture signaling assays and zebrafish model
records.population: Cell cultures and zebrafish, no human clinical participants
outcomes: Fourteen compounds inhibited nitric oxide production in BV-2 cells
TLR4-associated signaling effects in preclinical models
records.uncertainty: No human efficacy, dosing, or safety conclusions can be drawn.
records.adverse_effects: No human adverse-event assessment; zebrafish model only.
records.interactions: Cell signaling studied; no herb-drug interaction tested.
records.limitations: Cellular and zebrafish outcomes do not establish human clinical relevance.
